question.problem: Find the equation of the level curve that passes through the point $F(\sqrt{7},1)$ for the function $f(x,y)=\frac{12y}{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $F$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\sqrt{7},1) & =\frac{12(1)}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}-{1}^{2}}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the level curve that passes through $F(\sqrt{7},1)$ is the $2$-level curve.

Recall that the level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=2.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ \frac{12y}{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}} & =2 \\ 6y & ={x}^{2}-{y}^{2} \\ -{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+6y & =0 \\ -{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+6y+9 & =9 \\ -{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level curve that passes through $F(\sqrt{7},1)$ is the hyperbola $-{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}=9.$
